title: Prayer
definition: Prayer is communicating with God through worship, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, dependence, and fellowship.
summary: Prayer is the believer's ongoing relationship and communication with God through Christ.
christFocus: Jesus teaches His people to pray, gives them access to the Father, and intercedes for them as the risen Savior.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Prayer is not a religious performance but communion with the living God. Through Christ, believers come before the Father with reverence, honesty, dependence, worship, confession, thanksgiving, and request.

Prayer is shaped by Scripture and strengthened by the Holy Spirit. Believers pray because God hears, cares, rules, provides, corrects, comforts, and invites His children to draw near.

Prayer does not manipulate God or bend Him to human will. It teaches the heart to trust the Father, seek His kingdom, depend on His grace, and walk with Him in all circumstances.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many believers try to carry burdens alone or only pray when crisis comes. Prayer matters because it keeps the heart dependent on God instead of self-sufficient, anxious, or spiritually isolated.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Build a steady rhythm of prayer that includes worship, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, and honest requests. Bring your needs to God through Christ and let prayer reshape your desires around His will.
